verifiers.evidence:
Evidence: I read `docs/agents/adjudications/FP-0001/case.json`, the flagged file `packages/ui/src/components/VirtualSelect/VirtualSelect.component.tsx` (100 lines), `.fallowrc.json`, `reports/fallow/baselines/health.json` and the fallow skill docs under `.github/skills/fallow-code-checker/`. `VirtualSelect` is a single arrow function that runs straight through. It takes destructured props, six of them with default values (`isAlwaysOpen`, `isBusy`, `isDisabled`, `options`, `placeholder`, `shouldFillHeight`). It makes one call to `useVirtualSelect` and returns JSX that passes values to `VirtualSelectProvider` and four child components. The only control flow anywhere in the body is one ternary, `shouldFillHeight ? styles.containerFill : undefined`, on line 90. It has no `if`, loop, `switch`, `&&`/`||` rendering, `break`/`continue`, early return or nested callback. The analyzer agrees: it reports `cyclomatic: 2`, which is exactly one decision point. The rule's own explanation says it uses the SonarSource cognitive complexity method. Under that method this ternary scores +1 at nesting 0, because JSX elements, object literals and calls like `stylex.props(...)` don't add nesting. So the function should score about 1, far from the reported 16. The method only adds nesting on top of the control-flow increments, and every one of those also counts toward cyclomatic complexity, so a function with cyclomatic 2 cannot honestly reach 16. The extra 15 must come from things that aren't control flow, probably the default parameters, JSX depth or the 18 props. Those are not the hard-to-follow branching the rule exists to catch. I couldn't confirm the cause because the fallow source isn't in the tree and the case has no trace (`"trace": null`). The suggested fix, extracting helpers, has also already been done: the branching lives in `./hooks` (`useVirtualSelect`) and the `VirtualSelectLabel`, `Header`, `Dropdown` and `HiddenInputs` subcomponents. `.fallowrc.json` sets no lower cognitive threshold or override for this path that would explain the result some other way.

Check: The finding would be real if this function had hidden control flow: conditional rendering with `&&`/`||`/`??` chains, nested ternaries, inline callbacks with branches, or loops or early returns in its body. It would also be real if the `<template>`/`<component>` rollup modes, which add a template's score to a function's, applied here. I searched `packages/ui/src/components/VirtualSelect/VirtualSelect.component.tsx` line by line and found only the one ternary on line 90. The rollup modes only cover Angular, Vue, Svelte and Astro templates, not a `.tsx` function. `.fallowrc.json` has no `health.thresholdOverrides` entry or rule override matching this file. None of these is present.

Evidence:
- The case file reports `VirtualSelect` at cognitive complexity 16, with `exceeded: "cognitive"`. The default limit is 15, as `docs/tooling/fallow-summary.md` states.
- `.fallowrc.json` sets no `maxCognitive` for the `health` section as a whole. None of its `thresholdOverrides` covers `packages/ui/src/components/VirtualSelect/`. They cover tests, repo-standards scripts and eslint-local-rules only. The default limit therefore applies to this file.
- I read `VirtualSelect.component.tsx`. The function is a 17-property destructured parameter with 5 default values, one hook call, one ternary and one JSX tree. The score is mostly default-value branching plus a large prop surface. That makes it a borderline, mildly inflated measurement, but the rule is working as defined and the value is over the limit.
- ADR-032 says to read `exceeded`. A `cognitive` finding is real complexity, not a coverage artifact like `crap`-only findings.
- The evidence is balanced at best, and the instructions say to rule REAL in that case.

Fix: In `VirtualSelect.component.tsx`, remove the inline destructuring defaults from the `VirtualSelect` signature. They are `isAlwaysOpen = false`, `isBusy = false`, `isDisabled = false`, `options = []`, `placeholder = 'Select...'` and `shouldFillHeight = false`.
1. Take `props: VirtualSelectProps` instead.
2. Let `useVirtualSelect` apply the defaults for `isAlwaysOpen`, `isBusy`, `isDisabled` and `options`, and return the resolved values.
3. Apply `placeholder` and `shouldFillHeight` in the hook too, or in a small `resolveVirtualSelectProps(props)` helper in `./hooks`. Either way the component body no longer carries the default branching.
4. Move the `shouldFillHeight ? styles.containerFill : undefined` ternary into a helper, or into the hook's return value as a `containerStyle`.
5. Re-run fallow to confirm the score is at or below 15.

Do not add a suppression comment. That would hide the finding without changing the code.

Evidence:
- `packages/ui/src/components/VirtualSelect/VirtualSelect.component.tsx` lines 13–100: the flagged function destructures 18 props (6 with literal defaults), calls one custom hook (`useVirtualSelect`) with an object literal, and returns one JSX tree (`VirtualSelectProvider > div > 4 leaf delegates`) whose attributes are plain object literals. The only decision point in the whole body is `shouldFillHeight ? styles.containerFill : undefined` at line 90. No `if`, loop, `switch`, `catch`, early return, boolean-operator sequence, nested function, label jump or recursion.
- Hand-scored against the SonarSource Cognitive Complexity spec the rule cites ("penalizes nesting depth and non-linear control flow"): the ternary is +1 with no nesting increment, because it sits inside no control-flow structure or nested function (JSX elements, object literals, call arguments and destructuring defaults are not nesting or increment constructs in the spec). Score = 1. Fallow's own `cyclomatic: 2` in the case file confirms there is exactly one branch; under the spec a cognitive score of 16 with a single branch is impossible, since every nesting penalty must attach to a structural increment that would also raise cyclomatic.
- `.fallowrc.json`: `health` sets `maxUnitSize` and `thresholdOverrides` that only *raise* limits for scripts/tests; no override lowers `maxCognitive` for `packages/ui/**`, so the threshold is the default 15 (`docs/tooling/fallow-summary.md` line 65). No configuration makes a score-1 function exceed it.
- `reports/fallow/baselines/health.json`: the only `complexity_*` finding in the tracked baseline is in `scripts/refresh-fallow-complexity-report.cjs`. Sibling components of the same or greater structural complexity are absent from it: `packages/ui/src/components/NavLink/NavLink.component.tsx` (7 destructured defaults, 2 ternaries, 2 `&&` JSX guards, `||`, an `if` early return and a nested arrow — genuinely ~8–10 cognitive) and `packages/ui/src/components/SidePanel/SidePanel.component.tsx` (ternary with `&&`, conditional spread, `if`). The shape fallow flagged here is not one it scores above 15 elsewhere in the package.
- `packages/ui/src/components/VirtualSelect/hooks/useVirtualSelect.hook.ts`: the real derivation logic (`??`, `===`, `||`, ternary, `if` in a nested handler) lives in a separate function that fallow scores on its own and did not flag; nothing was folded into the shell. `contexts/VirtualSelectContext.provider.tsx` is equally linear.
- `packages/ui/src/components/VirtualSelect/VirtualSelect.component.test.tsx`: 12 `it` cases exercise single/multi selection, busy state, outside click, `onFetchInitial`, hidden inputs and the label through the shell — behaviour is covered and reveals no hidden control flow.
- The finding is a plain function finding (`name: "VirtualSelect"`, no `<component>`/`<template>` unit, no `component_rollup`), so the template/rollup variants described in the explanation do not apply. `react_prop_count: 18` is reported but is not what `exceeded: cognitive` measures; the rule's own "How to fix" (extract helpers, split branches, flatten guards) has nothing to act on — there is one branch and no guards.

Check: (1) Hand-applied the SonarSource cognitive rules to every construct in `packages/ui/src/components/VirtualSelect/VirtualSelect.component.tsx` looking for any increment beyond the line-90 ternary — found none; score 1, consistent with fallow's own `cyclomatic: 2`. (2) Searched `.fallowrc.json` for a `thresholdOverrides`/`health` entry lowering `maxCognitive` for `packages/ui` that would make a low score fail — none; only raises exist. (3) Searched `reports/fallow/baselines/health.json` for complexity findings on `packages/ui/src/components/NavLink/NavLink.component.tsx`, `packages/ui/src/components/SidePanel/SidePanel.component.tsx` and `packages/ui/src/components/Table/shared/ColumnWidthPresetButtons/ColumnWidthPresetButtons.component.tsx` (same destructured-default + JSX shape, equal or more branching) — absent, so the shape does not score >15 in fallow elsewhere. (4) Read `packages/ui/src/components/VirtualSelect/hooks/useVirtualSelect.hook.ts` and `contexts/VirtualSelectContext.provider.tsx` for control flow that might have been inlined into the shell — it is separate and unflagged. (5) Read `packages/ui/src/components/VirtualSelect/VirtualSelect.component.test.tsx` and the callers in `packages/ui/src/components/Form/fields/SelectField/SelectField.component.tsx`, `Table/filters/FilterInputs/OperatorSelect/OperatorSelect.component.tsx`, `Table/filters/SelectFilterInput/SelectFilterInput.component.tsx`, `Table/TableSettingsDrawer/FiltersSection/AddFilterSection/AddFilterSection.component.tsx`, `.../AddGroupKeySection.component.tsx`, `.../AddSortSection.component.tsx` for any input or prop that changes the function's control flow — complexity is static and no caller adds a branch. (6) Searched `.github/skills/fallow-code-checker/CONFIGURATION.md`, `docs/tooling/fallow-summary.md`, `docs/decisions/ADR-032-real-coverage-for-the-fallow-gate.md` and `scripts/refresh-fallow-complexity-report.cjs` for any documented fallow rule that charges destructured defaults, JSX depth or object-literal attributes toward cognitive complexity — none documented; the 16 cannot be derived from the cited definition, and the repo's own triage note (CONFIGURATION.md line 274) says `exceeded: cognitive` should mean "genuinely complex", which this straight-line shell is not.
